chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: Ken Murray hires him for the Blackouts
summary: Ken Murray hears the broadcast and buys the contract; Mosley is in the Blackouts for about nine months.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Then we all heard the word that Ken Murray was looking for somebody to go in the Black-outs. I had no idea that I would ever get--Benny Carter would give his right arm--everybody was trying for it. The guy that was playing along with me was Wingy Manone.
Wingy Manone was playing opposite you?
he's around too. Those guys had a beautiful trio; man, we had to really blow.

One night, in walked Ken Murray and he came up to the bandstand and said, I'm Ken Murray; almost knocked me over. He impressed me. I just heard you on the air--he was on his way home and we were broadcasting and he said to himself--later on he told me--he said this is what I think I need. He came in there and obviously we impressed him. He bought my contract from Billy Berg.
How long did you stay with Ken Murray's Blackouts?
I was in his Blackouts for about nine months. That was something. It was the longest running and the biggest production in the history of Hollywood.
